documents.abstract: An electromagnetic (EM) digital twin gives mobile robots wireless situational awareness but depends on material conductivities that change with the environment. Online calibration faces initialization sensitivity and measurement travel costs. We demonstrate a vision-language model (VLM)-guided framework using a Unitree G1 robot and NVIDIA Sionna, with two VLM calls: material classification maps visible materials through ITU-R P.2040 to conductivity priors for Sionna's gradient descent on accumulated received signal strength (RSS) measurements; waypoint planning selects the next measurement location online using residual RSS calibration error and image coverage. In a real indoor scenario, the framework achieves a normalized mean absolute conductivity error of $1.74\times10^{-4}$ within 20 m of travel; random initialization never converges, while random waypoints require over twice the travel.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the delivery of academic support services through intelligent conversational systems capable of providing timely and accurate responses to users. Traditional methods of obtaining information within higher education institutions often rely on manual interactions with administrative staff, resulting in delays, increased workload, and limited accessibility outside official working hours. This study presents the design and implementation of an intelligent-based chatbot for Al-Hikmah University to automate responses to students' academic enquiries. The chatbot was developed using a retrieval-based architecture integrated with Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to understand user queries and retrieve relevant responses from an institutional knowledge base. The system was implemented using React.js for the frontend, Node.js and Express.js for the backend, MongoDB as the database management system, and Google's Gemini API to enhance conversational intelligence. Functional and usability evaluations were conducted using representative student queries covering admission, registration, course information, tuition fees, examinations, and academic regulations. Experimental results demonstrated that the chatbot provides 98% accurate responses with low response within one to two seconds latency while remaining available twenty-four hours a day. The proposed system improves accessibility to institutional information, reduces the workload on administrative personnel, and enhances students' overall experience. The study concludes that AI-powered academic chatbots can significantly improve digital service delivery in Nigerian universities and recommends future integration with voice recognition, multilingual support, and student information systems.

This chapter traces the evolution of usability from its focus on physical measurements to addressing more complex cultural considerations, advocating for design as an organic set of conditions rather than static endpoints. It challenges designers to move beyond controlling users and toward discovering new design possibilities through unexpected uses and manipulations. The chapter identifies three waves of usability development. First-wave usability focused on physical experience through ergonomics and human factors design. Henry Dreyfuss pioneered measuring design against human body dimensions, while Niels Diffrient’s Humanscale attempted generalities. However, these standards revealed inherent biases based predominantly on Western white male statistics, with problematic historical connections including Ernst Neufert’s work for the Third Reich. The concept of “extreme users”—those with varying abilities, sizes, or ages—emerged to combat these biases, though empathy suits still fail to capture emotional and cognitive dimensions. Second-wave usability introduced human-centered design as cognitive study. Donald Norman’s The Design of Everyday Things established foundational concepts bridging the “gulf of knowledge” (knowledge “in the head” versus “in the world”) and the “gulf of execution.” Affordances became central—including perceived, hidden, anti-, and false affordances. Perceived affordances focus on what the user perceives can be done, whether or not that feature exists; hidden affordances remain undiscovered by users; anti-affordances intentionally prevent actions (like speed bumps or hostile architecture’s spikes preventing homeless people from resting); false affordances create the illusion of action without the effect. The perception at the center of the use of affordances relies on schemas—mental constructs from cultural experiences— which allow users to apply previous knowledge to new situations. Third-wave usability examines cultural and contextual experiences in life-centered design. Design anthropology emerged within this wave to better understand how cultural attitudes affect design usability, challenging colonial mindsets in both anthropology and design practice. Elizabeth Tunstall’s Decolonizing Design advocates for designers to question biases, “listen first,” and cede power to communities, shifting from extractive data-gathering toward mutually beneficial, reciprocal relationships that acknowledge design’s role in shaping future cultures.

Although many technologies have advanced in electricity production, their carbon footprint remains a crucial factor in selecting the most sustainable option. Solar energy provides a promising solution, as it is a clean and renewable resource harnessed directly from the sun. Multi-layer type thermal absorbers are considered the most effective structures, and their efficiency can be further enhanced with the incorporation of advanced materials such as graphene and MXene. In the current study, the solar absorber is fabricated using Cr-Fe₃O₄-InSb materials, with a thin graphene film added to enhance overall thermal performance. The design features two square structures with a cylindrical resonator inserted at the center. The proposed structure achieves an impressive thermal absorption rate of 93.28% through a broad wavelength range of up to 2800 nm. Specifically, the structure can be configured to achieve a thermal absorption rate of 90.9%, 93.32%, and 94.72% for UV-Vis-NIR regions while maintaining these rates across the respective ranges: 90.9% in the ultraviolet, 93.32% in the visible, and 94.72% in the NIR, with the polarization-insensitive property applicable for incidence angles from 0 to 80 degrees. To extract precise performance values based on regression analysis for varying layer heights, machine learning techniques for a 0.25 test size and the R² value reach above 0.98. As a thermal energy innovation, the proposed absorber can be utilized in various thermal processes, including water heaters, cookers, solar ponds, fuel production, coffee roasters, swimming pool heating, and more.

Why can an organisation invest in people, learning and technology, meet its performance targets, and still depend on particular individuals to keep work moving? Successful outcomes can conceal missing information, unclear decision authority and disconnected processes when capable employees compensate for weaknesses in the arrangements surrounding their work. Designing for Organisational Capability: From Intended Outcomes to Sustained Performance examines how organisations can deliberately design the conditions through which required outcomes are produced, sustained and adapted. Building on From Workforce to Organisational Capability, it develops an outcome-first approach that connects people, work, information, authority, learning, support and technology around the performance the organisation needs to achieve. A continuing illustrative service-team case carries the argument from defining the intended outcome to tracing work, strengthening interfaces and creating the conditions for workplace application. The paper then examines the relationship between human judgement and AI, how evidence makes performance evident, and how organisations build the capacity to adapt as operating conditions change. The discussion draws on research into training transfer, informal learning, organisational design, generative AI and dynamic capabilities, alongside NIST’s AI Risk Management Framework. It distinguishes these research foundations from the Capability Design applications developed within the paper. Written for leaders, learning and development professionals, work designers and organisational practitioners, the whitepaper offers a basis for examining whether investments have established dependable capability and what must work together for intended outcomes to become sustained performance. Part of the Capability Excellence™ Whitepaper Series.

documents.abstract: The research is devoted to the issue of creating a safe and reliable artificial intelligence (AI) system. Objective: to create a clear list of requirements for future standards in the field of ethics of artificial intelligence in order to bridge the gap between theory and practice. Methods: methods of induction and synthesis, comparative analysis and analogy are used. Results: an analysis of the existing guidelines on AI ethics was carried out and it was concluded that it contains mainly general recommendations, without specific technical rules. Possible errors and the reasons for the difficulty of holding potentially responsible parties accountable in the field of AI implementation are presented. A three-component list of requirements for artificial intelligence technologies and the relevant data on the basis of which they are defined has been developed; a step-by-step plan for integrating ethical principles into practical aspects of development and regulation has been proposed. The practical significance lies in offering a framework for national and international regulatory documents that will ensure the safe use of the technology and increase user confidence.

documents.abstract: Conspectus Today we are experiencing an unprecedentedly rapid transformation of science, driven by advances in computing and artificial intelligence (AI). At the same time, there are growing cumulative pressures of climate change impacts that not only affect economies but are creating significant societal challenges. The confluence of technology push and environmental–socioeconomic pressures is promoting the development of sustainable chemistry. The link between the transition to sustainability in chemistry and the digital transformation of R&D and manufacturing has been the long-standing focus in our research (Fantke, P.; et al. Chem 2021, 7, 2866 doi: 10.1016/j.chempr.2021.09.012). Sustainability is not a feature of a single chemical product or a process. It is incorrect to talk about “sustainable polyethylene”, as such narrow framing will miss many issues in the more holistic system that not only includes the cradle-to-grave life cycle emission impacts of polyethylene but also considers all aspects of equity, impact on biodiversity, resilience of supply chains, etc. Sustainable chemistry makes sense only as a complex system. An analysis of complex systems requires large amounts of data and the use of appropriate analytical tools, such as advanced machine learning techniques. The chemical industry has been an early adopter of digital technologies, motivated by the inherent complexity of chemical systems and the need for efficiency to stay economically competitive. As early as the 1970s, cheminformatics tools were introduced to support structure–property analysis. In the 1980s, we saw the broad adoption of process modeling and simulation tools for design, scale-up, and optimization of chemical processes, paralleled with developments in the field of process system engineering and control. Today’s digital transition is much deeper; everything from scientific discovery (molecules, materials, and phenomena) to chemical process development, analytical methods and process analytical technologies, and plant operation is being reshaped. This deep transformation includes the development of a radically different approach to data in chemistry. Advances in self-driving laboratories, agentic AI workflows, and digital factories require access to structured, semantically rich data. In this Account, we focus on three key areas of digitalization and AI technologies advancing chemistry and chemical process development toward net-zero targets. First, we discuss how data mining tools are used to analyze the existing value chains and identify opportunities to integrate net-zero feedstocks. When new molecules are introduced, data-driven route planning can be employed to design alternative synthetic pathways, which then need to be rigorously evaluated. Second, we focus on how to use AI to accelerate discoveries in chemistry, including the innovative design of catalysts, rational selection of solvents, and identification of optimal reaction conditions. By leveraging statistical modeling and data-driven optimization, these traditionally time-consuming tasks can now be performed much faster. Lastly, we discuss how to bring these innovations from the laboratory to manufacturing, which also requires advances in process technologies. We show that by leveraging AI agents, process modeling, and knowledge graphs, there is a potential to achieve automated process design and life cycle assessment, removing traditional choke points in scaling technologies and providing timely support for decision-making in early-stage development. In the end, we discuss the current challenges and future perspectives.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Patients with rheumatic diseases have persistent information needs that are not fully addressed in routine care. We developed and evaluated guideline-grounded, large language model (LLM) chatbots to support patient self-management and education in rheumatology.Ten disease-specific chatbots based on German guidelines were co-developed and deployed through 13 rheumatology centres and six patient organisations. Chatbot users rated responses and completed a questionnaire. User questions, feedback, and response characteristics were analysed using category-based coding and a six-dimensional LLM-as-a-judge assessment, with LLM-based ratings compared with rheumatologist ratings in random subsets.Between September 2025 and January 2026, 6291 questions were recorded. Thirteen question categories were identified, most commonly disease-specific questions (50.2%), medication and monitoring (37.3%) and diagnostics (28.2%). The chatbots were unable to answer in 263 interactions (4.2%). Of 2671 responses rated by users, 2481 (92.9%) received a positive rating. Insufficient detail was the most common reason for negative ratings (125/190, 65.8%). Among 602 questionnaire respondents, 84.6% reported that the chatbot was easy to use, 84.1% that answers were easy to understand, and 80.2% that it was a useful addition to patient education. In the LLM-based evaluation, 95.3% of answers were rated as completely safe and 79.1% as completely correct. Guideline adherence was assessed separately, with 45.0% rated as fully adherent; agreement with physician assessment was weak.Guideline-grounded chatbots received predominantly positive user feedback in real-world use, while LLM-based evaluation suggested that most responses were safe and correct. User questions and feedback may help guide iterative improvements to source content and patient education materials. Further studies are needed to evaluate educational effectiveness and independently validate response quality and clinical safety.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Background The rapid expansion of digital technologies is transforming health systems and creating increasing demand for a workforce with competencies in health informatics, data science, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, digital health governance, and implementation. However, digital health training remains fragmented in many low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), including Tanzania. This study describes the systematic, evidence-based process used to develop an MSc Digital Health program at Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences (MUHAS), Tanzania. Methods A mixed-methods curriculum development approach was undertaken, comprising document review and benchmarking, a quantitative stakeholder survey, qualitative interviews with alumni of the MSc Health Information Management program, and a stakeholder consultative workshop. Nine higher-education and competency-framework sources were reviewed to identify gaps and emerging competency domains. A structured survey was administered to 48 stakeholders purposively selected from government, non-governmental, private-sector, and start-up organizations. Qualitative data from alumni interviews and open-ended survey responses were analyzed thematically using manual coding by two independent coders. A two-day consultative workshop involving 22 stakeholders from academia, professional associations, non-governmental organizations, government, and clinical practice reviewed and validated the proposed curriculum. Results Benchmarking demonstrated substantial variability in digital health curriculum content, with no single program comprehensively covering all priority competency domains. Stakeholders identified AI and machine learning (48.0%) and big data and analytics (41.7%) as prominent emerging technology competencies, while data science and predictive analytics, health information systems and interoperability, cybersecurity and data privacy, and epidemiology and biostatistics were also emphasized. Overall, 81.3% of survey respondents considered digital health competencies highly important to their organizations, while 89.6% indicated willingness to employ MUHAS MSc Digital Health graduates. Qualitative findings emphasized five priority areas: advanced computing and emerging technologies; applied health data science and analytics; health systems architecture and interoperability; experiential learning and program delivery; and governance, cybersecurity, leadership, and professional ethics. Workshop participants endorsed the proposed curriculum and recommended stronger practical learning, field attachment, innovation-oriented projects, and alignment of course content with emerging workforce needs. The resulting program was structured as a two-year, full-time MSc Digital Health program with three specialization tracks: Digital Health Leadership, Digital Health Systems Development, and Health Data Science and AI. Conclusion The MUHAS MSc Digital Health curriculum was developed through an iterative, evidence-informed, and stakeholder-driven process that integrates multidisciplinary digital health competencies with practical, implementation-oriented learning. The approach provides a potentially adaptable model for curriculum development in LMIC settings. Future evaluation should assess program implementation, graduate competencies, employment outcomes, employer satisfaction, and contribution to national digital health transformation.
topics: Information Systems Education and Curriculum Development

documents.abstract: Relevance . The analysis of existing practices regarding the elimination of medical and sanitary emergency consequences has revealed several challenges in the operation of regional Disaster Medicine Services (DMS) of the Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation. Research-based approaches to DMS further development and improvement are undoubtedly pivotal to improve preparedness within disaster medicine institutions by establishing ad hoc emergency response units capable of efficient medical care provision in case of emergency, including emergency medical care. The study aim is to outline the most promising perspectives for further DMS development and improvement by analyzing the years-long experience in medical care provision to eliminate medical and sanitary emergency consequences in the Russian Federation. Materials and methods . We studied the current regulatory and legal framework of the Russian Federation, research publications, the present DMS across regions, as well as the extensive practical experience of healthcare workers and DMS units in medical care provision within emergency response efforts. The study utilized historical and analytical methods, content analysis, expert assessment, contrastive and systemic analysis, comparison, and scientific synthesis. Results and discussion . Based on the DMS requirements, 10 fundamental conceptual approaches were developed to advance and improve the existing organizational structure across Russian Federation constituents, as well as underpin relevant management decisions regarding the assets and resources. The essence and content of the proposed approaches are elaborated; promising areas for DMS development in constituents of the Russian Federation have been identified. A retrospective analysis of response efforts to medical and sanitary consequences caused by the most critical and high-profile large-scale emergencies with mass sanitary losses in our country has been conducted with regard to the proposed approaches. Conclusion . The principal strategic direction for further development and improvement of regional DMS should include augmented efficiency of the service management system, optimized regulatory, legal, and methodological support, improved organizational and functional DMS and staffing structure across its units, as well as enhanced professional competencies in medical triage among healthcare workers, transformed approaches to logistics and material resource supply, and integrated artificial intelligence, information technologies, software platforms, and decision-support systems into DMS management processes.

Acute appendicitis remains the most common cause of acute abdomen and is associated with serious complications such as perforation if not diagnosed promptly. While laboratory tests and clinical findings are essential, their interpretation can be challenging and sometimes misleading. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, has shown promise in supporting clinical decision-making and enhancing diagnostic accuracy. This study aimed to evaluate the ability of ChatGPT-5 to predict the likelihood of appendicitis using clinical data, with diagnoses confirmed by histopathology and comparing it to Alvarado score which is most commonly known clinical scoring system to diagnose acute appendicitis. This retrospective comparative study evaluated the performance of ChatGPT-5 in predicting acute appendicitis across two phases. In Phase 1, the model was tested without prior context learning (i.e., without exposure to any previously labeled cases) to simulate real-world use of readily available LLMs. In Phase 2, it was re-tested after exposure to confirmed case outcomes. A structured prompting strategy was applied, incorporating patient demographics, clinical symptoms, laboratory data, and clinical context, with fixed output constraints across all cases. The dataset was divided into 70% (114 cases) for Phase 1 evaluation and 30% (48 cases) for Phase 2 validation. To address potential order leakage- a bias arising when predictions depend on case sequence rather than clinical reasoning- the cases were assessed both with and without randomization. Paired comparisons of sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy between ChatGPT-5 and the Alvarado score were performed using McNemar’s test, and Cohen’s kappa was used to assess agreement. In Phase 1, ChatGPT-5 without randomization achieved a sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 81.6%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 91.6%, negative predictive value (NPV) of 100%, and overall accuracy of 93.9%, compared with the Alvarado score (sensitivity 67.1%, specificity 92.1%, PPV 94.4%, NPV 58.3%, accuracy 75.4%). In Phase 2, ChatGPT-5 without randomization reached a sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 93.8%, PPV of 97.0%, NPV of 100%, and accuracy of 97.9%, comparable to the Alvarado score (sensitivity 96.9%, specificity 93.8%, PPV 96.9%, NPV 93.8%, accuracy 95.8%). Within this retrospective, surgically confirmed cohort with a high clinical suspicion of acute appendicitis, ChatGPT-5 showed high diagnostic sensitivity for excluding acute appendicitis when guided by an optimized prompt, even without prior context learning. Proper randomization of prompt data appears essential to minimize order leakage and to provide a more conservative and reliable estimate of model performance. ChatGPT-5 cannot yet be relied upon to confirm acute appendicitis, given the higher specificity of the Alvarado score, and its diagnostic sensitivity remained largely unaffected by context learning, with only a modest, non-significant gain in specificity. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation in a broader emergency-department population before any clinical implementation.

documents.abstract: This paper proposes the theory of Digital Exaptation (디지털 굴절적응) to resolve the foundational debate surrounding emergent reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs). Contemporary artificial intelligence discourse often views higher-order reasoning either as an unpredictable artifact of empirical scaling laws or dismisses it as mere statistical mimicry ("stochastic parrot"). Borrowing from evolutionary biologist Stephen Jay Gould’s concept of exaptation—wherein a trait evolved for one primary adaptive function is co-opted for an entirely novel utility (e.g., feathers evolving for thermoregulation before being exapted for aerodynamic flight)—we argue that reasoning in foundation models is not a teleologically designed objective, but an exaptive structural byproduct of hyper-dimensional statistical compression. By reframing LLM emergence through evolutionary biology, this paper bridges empirical machine learning and the philosophy of mind.

This chapter examines the rapidly evolving role of Digital Twins in the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction industry, emphasizing their integration with Human-Centric Artificial Intelligence, ISO 19650 information management, and Industry 5.0 principles. Digital Twins, continuously updated through Building Information Management, IoT sensing, and AI analytics enable real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and lifecycle optimization. The chapter highlights foundational frameworks such as the Gemini Principles, ISO 23247, and human-in-the-loop approaches that ensure transparency, trust, and explainability in Digital Twin-driven decisions. Critical challengesincluding cybersecurity vulnerabilities, semantic interoperability, and ethical governanceare addressed through zero-trust architectures, ontology-based data models, explainable Artificial Intelligence, and blockchain-enabled auditability. The chapter further explores how Digital Twins support sustainability and the circular economy via material passports, carbon tracking, and resource-efficient lifecycle strategies. Case studies demonstrate measurable benefits in safety, energy performance, and predictive analytics, positioning Digital Twins as central to human-centric, resilient, and sustainable Construction 6.0 ecosystems.

Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (AI) conversational agents are increasingly used for everyday, non-clinical mental-health support, yet little is known about when these exchanges feel fitting and comfortable. We used a laboratory mixed-methods design to examine associations among perceived convenience of interaction (PCI), relational attitude (RA), willingness to self-disclose (WSD), anthropomorphism (AN), perceived fit/comfort (FC), and thinking style in 83 participants (43 rational-dominant; 40 experiential-dominant). WSD showed the strongest unique association with FC. A post hoc reverse model also found a unique FC-WSD association, leaving their temporal order unresolved. AN had no stable direct association with FC, but the WSD-FC association became stronger as AN increased. Group comparisons and continuous Rational-Experiential Inventory (REI) analyses converged: relatively stronger experiential processing was associated with higher AN, whereas relatively stronger rational processing was associated with higher WSD. The group-blind thematic analysis linked disclosure decisions to privacy, control, social distance, functional usefulness, and affective comfort. Together, the findings identify WSD as a key correlate of FC and show that anthropomorphism conditions this association rather than simply improving the interaction. Clear boundaries, controllability, and adjustable relational cues therefore warrant attention in future design research.

This research aims to explore the nature of left-handed children and identify the necessary conditions for their effective preparation for school. The study analyzes the brain activity of left-handed children, specifically their unique characteristics in visual imagery and spatial perception. The research provides a scientific rationale regarding the negative neuropsychological and pedagogical consequences of forcibly retraining left-handed children to use their right hand. Additionally, the author has developed methodological recommendations for developing graphic skills, organizing an ergonomic workspace, and the use of specialized educational tools designed for left-handed students.

This work aims to develop a domain-adapted Bengali text summarization model by training and fine-tuning on general and domain-specific datasets with categories such as state, international, and sports. Flan-T5 and mT5 LLMs were trained on the XLSUM Bengali dataset for text summarization, and they were trained on source domains and fine-tuned on the target domains for domain adaptation. In general-domain summarization on the XLSum Bengali dataset, mT5 achieved stronger overall performance than Flan-T5, with ROUGE-1 and BERTScore values of 0.21 and 0.72, respectively. The Flan-T5-XLSUM model outperformed other LLMs, achieving a ROUGE score of 0.79, a BLEU score of 0.13 and a BERTScore of 0.86. A human evaluation involving 28 participants was conducted to assess summary fluency, adequacy, and factual consistency across domains, confirming the qualitative effectiveness of the proposed models. A custom dataset is developed with manually annotated categories for domain adaptation purposes, contributing to domain-specific Bengali data. The ablation study illustrated that pre-training and fine-tuning on domain-specific data significantly enhanced model performance, with Flan-T5 fine-tuned on sports data. Three explainability methods (LIME, SHAP, and BertViz) revealed that geographically and contextually meaningful tokens strongly influenced the domain-adaptive Flan-T5 Bengali summarization model. The adapter-based Flan-T5 architecture enables effective multi-domain fine-tuning with less than 1% of trainable parameters while preserving model performance.

Introduction This study examines the relationships among Organizational Culture, Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Management, and Organizational Performance in manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) operating within construction supply chains in Norte de Santander, Colombia. Methods We collected survey data from 204 employees across 16 manufacturing SMEs and analyzed them using structural equation modeling (SEM). The model evaluated the direct relationships among the three constructs and the indirect effect of Organizational Culture on Organizational Performance through OHS Management. Results The results indicate that Organizational Culture is positively associated with OHS Management and Organizational Performance, while OHS Management is positively associated with Organizational Performance. The bootstrapped indirect effect supports OHS Management's partial mediating role. Discussion These findings suggest that Organizational Culture is associated with performance through two complementary pathways: a direct pathway involving shared values, managerial commitment, communication, and organizational practices, and an indirect pathway involving the institutionalization of OHS management practices. The study contributes to the literature by positioning OHS Management as an organizational mechanism that helps explain how cultural conditions relate to performance outcomes. For manufacturing SMEs linked to construction supply chains, the findings highlight the importance of integrating cultural development with risk prevention, safety training, regulatory compliance, and employee participation. The results should be interpreted considering the cross-sectional design, the use of self-reported data, and the nesting of employees within a limited number of firms.
